questions.question: Which signal is the best starting SLI for a checkout promise that customers can complete payment?
options: Successful eligible payment authorizations divided by eligible authorization attempts
Average CPU utilization across application hosts
Number of dashboard panels
Total log bytes written per minute
questions.explanation: A success ratio directly measures the stated customer outcome. CPU and logs can help diagnose a problem but do not prove that payment completed.

questions.question: Why must an SLI define its eligible event population?
options: So the metric can include health checks and test traffic by default
So numerator and denominator describe the same promised behavior
So every metric has more label values
So percentile calculations are unnecessary
questions.explanation: An SLI is meaningful only when both parts count the same intended population. Mixing probes, retries, or unrelated events can hide or invent failure.

questions.question: A service has a 4% error rate for 12 minutes after a deployment. Why is this stronger page evidence than a 4% error rate for five seconds?
options: Twelve minutes consumes more of the user-impact and error-budget window
Any metric is correct only after twelve minutes
The request count no longer matters
CPU must be saturated after twelve minutes
questions.explanation: Persistence distinguishes a sustained harmful condition from a short transient. The exact window should follow the customer promise and response cost.

questions.question: Why can an average latency be unsafe as the only latency alert signal?
options: Averages cannot use milliseconds
A small group of very slow requests can be hidden by many fast requests
Percentiles are always lower than averages
Latency does not affect customers
questions.explanation: Tail percentiles expose the slower experiences that an average can smooth away, so they are often a better match for a user latency promise.

questions.question: Which label should generally stay out of a metric because it creates unbounded cardinality?
options: Region name from a fixed deployment list
HTTP route template such as /orders/:id
Raw request ID
Deployment version
questions.explanation: A raw request ID creates a new series for nearly every request. Put that identifier in traces or logs and retain bounded dimensions on metrics.

questions.question: A primary outcome metric stops reporting during a critical service outage. What policy is most defensible?
options: Assume the service is healthy because no errors are visible
Treat missing telemetry as an explicit observability condition and alert the appropriate owner
Delete the SLO because the data is incomplete
Page only when CPU exceeds 85%
questions.explanation: Missing evidence must have a defined meaning. A critical outcome signal that vanishes can hide an outage and should trigger observability investigation.
